text: Puberty (first oestrus) occurs between 1.5 and 3 years of age; body weight and growth, more than age alone, are the main factors controlling onset — poor nutrition can delay puberty. During oestrus the ovaries are active: after oestrus the ovary releases an ovule into the oviduct which can be fertilized by bull semen; days 2–4 the Corpus Luteum forms and secretes progesterone; if there is no fertilization the Corpus Luteum resorbs from day 5–17; day 21 a new ovule is released from a mature follicle, starting a new cycle. Without fertilization, oestrus recurs regularly, about every 17–24 days in zebu cattle (average 20–21 days), but each oestrus itself lasts only a few hours (average 12 hours in zebu), so farmers must watch closely not to miss it. Signs of oestrus include: licking and rubbing between cows, sniffing another cow's vagina, mutual chin resting, mounting or standing to be mounted, and clear vaginal discharge — all signs are more obvious when a bull is present.
